# Todo CLI

Build a command-line todo list in `todo.py` (Python 3 standard library only).
Run it as `python todo.py <command> [args]` from any directory. Items are stored in
`todo.json` in the current working directory as a JSON list of objects
`{"id": <int>, "text": <str>, "done": <bool>}` in id order. A missing file means an empty list.

Commands (stdout lines end with a newline; exit code 0 unless stated):

- `add TEXT` - add an item. Its id is 1 + the largest existing id (1 for an empty list).
  Print `added <id>: <text>`.
- `list` - print one line per item: `<id> [ ] <text>` (open) or `<id> [x] <text>` (done).
  Print `no items` when the list is empty.
- `done ID` - mark the item done and print `done <id>`.
- `remove ID` - delete the item and print `removed <id>`.
- For `done`/`remove` with an id that does not exist (or is not an integer), print
  `error: no item <ID>` to stderr and exit with code 1.
- Any other usage (no command, unknown command, missing argument) prints
  `usage: todo.py add TEXT | list | done ID | remove ID` to stderr and exits with code 2.

# Notes REST handler

Implement a tiny JSON REST API for notes in `app.py` using only the standard library
(`http.server`, `json`). Keep the routing logic in a pure function so it can be tested
without opening a socket.

1. `handle(method: str, path: str, body: bytes, store: dict) -> tuple[int, object]` returns
   `(status, payload)`. `store` maps note id (int) to the note dict and is modified in place.
   Notes are `{"id": <int>, "text": <str>}`.
   - GET on the collection path `/notes` -> 200 and the list of all notes sorted by id.
   - POST on `/notes` with a JSON object body `{"text": <non-empty string>}` -> 201 and the new
     note. Its id is 1 + the largest id in `store` (1 when empty). Anything else (invalid JSON,
     not an object, missing/empty/non-string text) -> 400 and `{"error": "invalid note"}`.
   - GET on `/notes/<id>` -> 200 and the note; DELETE on `/notes/<id>` -> 204 and payload
     `None`. A missing note or a non-integer id -> 404 and `{"error": "not found"}`.
   - Any other path -> 404 and `{"error": "not found"}`. A known path with an unsupported
     method (for example PUT on `/notes`) -> 405 and `{"error": "method not allowed"}`.
2. `class NotesHandler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler)` with `do_GET`, `do_POST`, `do_PUT`
   and `do_DELETE` that read the request body (Content-Length), call `handle` with the
   module-level `STORE` dict and write the payload as JSON with `Content-Type:
   application/json` (no body for 204).
3. `make_server(port: int = 0) -> http.server.HTTPServer` bound to 127.0.0.1 (port 0 picks a
   free port).

# Text statistics library

Implement the functions in `textstats.py` (standard library only). `test_textstats.py`
is the test specification; it must keep passing (`python test_textstats.py` exits 0).

A *word* is a maximal run of ASCII letters, digits and apostrophes ('). Words are compared
case-insensitively and reported in lower case.

- `word_count(text: str) -> int` - number of words.
- `char_frequency(text: str) -> dict[str, int]` - counts of the ASCII letters a-z in `text`,
  case-insensitive; only letters that occur are keys.
- `top_words(text: str, n: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]` - the `n` most frequent lower-cased
  words as (word, count) tuples, sorted by count (descending) then word (ascending).
  Returns [] when n <= 0.
- `average_word_length(text: str) -> float` - mean word length rounded to 2 decimals;
  0.0 when there are no words.
- `sentence_count(text: str) -> int` - each maximal run of `.`, `!` or `?` ends one sentence;
  if words appear after the last run (or there is no run at all) that trailing text counts
  as one more sentence. Text without words returns 0.
